decision: Use TypeScript/native page lifecycle events for a read-only observation display host; clear the source on mount, suspension, reactivation and disposal, and request one 20 ms refresh interval only while visible.
constraints: Offline browser DOM with a caller-owned admitted source and authorization; no new transport or credentials.
No queued views or personal identifiers; UNKNOWN remains current state; en and sv-SE panel guidance survives lifecycle changes.
Visibility/page suspension can delay or omit callbacks. Requested timer intervals are not real-time guarantees; a resumed view must not reuse observations admitted while inactive.

alternatives.assessment: Selected: expresses source/disposal contracts with static DOM checks and no deployed framework. The adapter controls the single timer and five listeners explicitly. The source remains a runtime-validated host boundary.
Equivalent execution capabilities; checked annotations or separate declarations are needed to preserve the same static consumer contract. No runtime speed advantage measured.

Provides hostConnected/hostDisconnected lifecycle composition. Page visibility, freeze and restored-page revocation still need explicit listeners independent of custom-element connection. A future component system may justify it; this adapter has no custom-element requirement.

Message-driven application model and JavaScript ports are credible for a full application. The source clearer, native page events and timer remain external subscriptions; no material advantage established for this small synchronous host boundary.

Typed foreign-function bindings can express event and timer APIs. They do not provide missing browser scheduling guarantees or source authorization, and no measured benefit justifies migration of this boundary.

limits: Synthetic event/clock tests in a structural DOM do not qualify browser navigation, back-forward cache, accessibility, OS suspend or installed product behavior.
The source must be exclusively owned by this host. The adapter does not stop ingress, abort sessions, revoke external copies, validate permission or reset producer state.
Source clearer or scheduler failure latches invalid guidance until remount. Reader failures withdraw displayed details and may recover on a later independent read.
No hard-real-time, hardware, weapon integration, MLS/CNSA, DDS/Link16, five-nines or tactical deployment claim.
No full application, searchable role-aware release-bound Help Center or P19 acceptance.
